SMTO-HTTP-0033 — SMTO couldn't unpack the service's reply

GUID: 6e4c8e25-5021-45a8-be42-8a2f3bab22ea
Slug: http-content-encoding-unsupported
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The service answered, but it compressed its reply in a way SMTO can't open, so SMTO didn't use it. If the request was meant to change something, the service may have done it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the task was changing something on the service, look there to see whether the change already happened before running it again. The service did answer, so it received the request; only its reply was unreadable.
  2. Open Parameter Store, select the HTTP connection, open Advanced connection settings, and remove any Default header named Accept-Encoding. That header can ask the service for a compression type SMTO can't read.
  3. Run the task again, asking for the same information in a plain, standard format, or from a different address on the service that returns ordinary data. SMTO reads only the common compression types, so a standard reply will come through.

What success looks like

  • The task's request returns readable data without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to whoever runs the service, asking whether it can reply without unusual compression. Don't treat the unreadable reply as a successful result.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The response Content-Encoding was not identity, gzip/x-gzip or deflate, or the compressed body contained concatenated/stacked streams, so the Gateway rejected the body.

What this means

  • Response Content-Encoding is outside identity, gzip/x-gzip or deflate, or a decoder found concatenated/stacked compressed data outside the supported representation. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Response Content-Encoding is outside identity, gzip/x-gzip or deflate, or a decoder found concatenated/stacked compressed data outside the supported representation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the public encoding header and whether the server used stacked or concatenated streams.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the response's Content-Encoding (for example br or zstd), remove any default Accept-Encoding header in the HTTP connection profile that requests it, or call an endpoint that returns identity, gzip or deflate as a single stream. Do not bypass the encoding check or treat the body as valid.
  • Request a supported content encoding or use an appropriate supported HTTP/file representation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The endpoint returns a complete supported single encoding within the byte bound.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
